title: Recognizing the First Correction
hook: The first pullback after BOS #1 sets the stage. It never holds the zone.

launchpad.outcome: Find Correction #1 on bullish and bearish charts, explain why it is never the execution zone, and apply the 15M reclaim rule as conditional, not mandatory.
launchpad.missionQuestion: How do you tell the first correction from everything around it?

takeaways: Correction #1 is the 5M pullback right after BOS #1.
A correction back toward the original 15M break is preferred.
Correction #1 never creates the execution zone. Correction #2 does.
A reclaim of the 15M level can add confirmation, but it is conditional, not mandatory.
remember: CORRECTION #1 SETS THE STAGE. IT NEVER HOLDS THE ZONE.

slides.headline: Find the first pullback.
slides.line: Correction #1 is the 5M pullback right after BOS (break of structure) #1. You’ll practise finding it on bullish and bearish charts.

cards.label: Where
cards.sub: Preferably back toward the original 15M break.

cards.label: What it isn’t
cards.sub: It never creates the execution zone. That’s Correction #2’s job.

slides.headline: Find Correction #1.
slides.line: BOS #1 has closed above the 15M level. Now find the first 5M pullback.
slides.why: That candle is part of the first 5M pullback after BOS #1.

after.caption: Correction #1 pulls back toward the 15M level before buyers push on.

slides.headline: Same job, other direction.
slides.line: BOS #1 has closed below the 15M level. In a bearish setup, Correction #1 pulls back up.
slides.why: That candle is part of the first 5M pullback after BOS #1, back up toward the 15M break.

after.caption: Correction #1 in a bearish setup is a move up, back toward the original 15M break.

slides.headline: Find it, then watch what follows.
slides.line: Bearish again. Find Correction #1, then see whether the sequence continues.
slides.why: That candle is part of the first 5M pullback after BOS #1.

after.caption: No BOS #2. Correction #1 formed, but no 5M candle closed below the low it pulled back from. The sequence is incomplete, so there is no trade.

slides.headline: Correction #1 is never the zone.
slides.line: Bullish example. Watch where the zone actually comes from.

steps.caption: Correction #1. A pullback, but not a zone. The sequence still needs BOS #2.
BOS #2. A 5M close above the high Correction #1 pulled back from.
Correction #2 creates the zone from its last bearish candle. This is where the zone lives.

check.prompt: Price later trades back into a Correction #1 candle. Is that your entry zone?

options.label: Yes, it’s a bearish candle in a pullback
options.feedback: Correction #1 never creates the execution zone. The zone comes from the last bearish candle of Correction #2.

options.label: No, the zone comes from Correction #2
options.why: Right. Correction #1 sets the stage. Correction #2 creates the zone.

slides.headline: Preferred, not mandatory.
slides.line: The reclaim rule is conditional and still under testing.

versus.label: Preferred
points: Correction #1 pulls back toward the original 15M break.
A reclaim of the 15M BOS or MSS (market structure shift) level can add structural confirmation.

versus.label: Not a requirement
points: The reclaim is a conditional rule, not a universal one.
Don’t reject an otherwise valid setup only because a reclaim didn’t happen.

check.prompt: Correction #1 pulled back toward the 15M break, but there was no reclaim of the 15M level. What do you do?

options.label: Reject the setup. The reclaim is required.
options.feedback: The reclaim can add confirmation, but it isn’t mandatory. Don’t reject an otherwise valid setup only because it didn’t happen.

options.label: Keep following the sequence
options.why: Right. A reclaim is extra confirmation when it happens. Keep reading for BOS #2, Correction #2 and BOS #3.

slides.quote: Correction #1 sets the stage. It never holds the zone.

slides.prompt: In your own words, how do you recognize Correction #1, and what role does the 15M reclaim play?
slides.modelAnswer: Correction #1 is the first 5M pullback right after BOS #1, preferably back toward the original 15M break. In a bullish setup it pulls down, and in a bearish setup it pulls up. It never creates the execution zone, because the zone comes from Correction #2. A reclaim of the 15M level can add confirmation, but it is conditional, so I don’t reject an otherwise valid setup just because it didn’t happen.
